doc.title: The Secret of Kohelet
doc.desc: An interactive adventure for children aged 8–15 and for adults (16+) based on Rabbi Shneor Ashkenazi’s lesson on the Book of Kohelet (Ecclesiastes). Find your chelek — the portion the Almighty gave you. No ads, no chats, your data stays on your device.

evening.options.t: Everything is great, I have enough
evening.options.r: Maybe. Remember this feeling: soon we will come back to it together.
That happens to almost everyone: the more you gather, the more you want. Strange, isn't it?

evening.options.t: A bit boring. As if something is missing
evening.options.r: You have everything, and yet something is missing. I wonder what exactly?

evening.options.t: I wish someone were with me
evening.options.r: So it turns out the most important thing can't be put in a treasure chest.

evening.options.t: I want to share it with someone
evening.options.r: Interesting: joy seems to become real only when you share it.
That's honest. Sometimes it takes time to understand what you feel.

book.label: Open the book
book.lead: In the very heart of the old library lies a book that nobody has been able to open. There is one word on the cover.
book.after: The pages are glowing. Letters fly out of the book, and on the first page a question appears…
treasure.say: Collect! Tap the {{what}} as fast as you can. And keep an eye on both bars.
treasure.hint: Just keep collecting and see how the second bar behaves.
treasure.full: The “Collected” bar is full. And what did you notice?
treasure.opts: I need to collect even more
I think the game is broken
treasure.resp: You noticed it yourself. What you have collected keeps growing, but the feeling of “enough” goes back to where it was.
Let's check: here are another hundred. The second bar still stays where it is. Interesting, isn't it?
The game is working. It isn't a mistake: that's how the second bar is made. I wonder why.
maslow.say: Don't rush after “even more.” King Shlomo once already tried everything. Place his experiments on the steps of Maslow's pyramid: choose an experiment, then a step. There are no right or wrong answers here.
maslow.label: Maslow's pyramid and Shlomo's experiments
maslow.cards: Gathered silver, gold and the treasures of kings
Became great, greater than all before him
maslow.level: Now choose a step. Tap an experiment on a step to take it back.
maslow.hint: There is no right answer here. Put each experiment where you think it helps a person most.
maslow.verdict: Shlomo looked back at everything he had done and said: “Behold, all is vapour and a chasing after the wind.” The lower steps are filled to the brim. But the top one, “Meaning,” has stayed empty.
maslow.verdictTop: Shlomo looked back at everything he had done and said: “Behold, all is vapour and a chasing after the wind.” Even what you put on the “Meaning” step Shlomo called vapour. The top step is empty again.
maslow.after: Shlomo rejects neither houses, nor gardens, nor wisdom. He is looking for what will fill the top step. His answer is still ahead.
timeline.say: Rav Ashkenazi says: all of history is a huge puzzle. Put a piece of it together: tap the events in order, from the most ancient to our own time.
timeline.label: History timeline
timeline.hint: First came the forefathers, then Moshe, then the kings. The last event happened in the 20th century.
timeline.later: This event happened later. Try another one.
timeline.events: Moshe hands the people over to Yehoshua
The women sing about Shaul and David
Shlomo speaks before the people in the Temple
Chizkiyahu and his company write down Kohelet
The kings of Judah · Bava Batra 15a
The Mishnah: “Who is rich? One who rejoices in his portion”
The sages of the Mishnah · Avot 4:1
The Baal Shem Tov: a soul comes into the world for one good deed
The Rebbe and Yitzchak Rabin talk about the mishnah “Who is rich?”
timeline.done: From Yaakov to our days: one picture, and every event in it is in its place. The next piece is yours. It is not your duty to finish the work, but neither are you free to withdraw from it.
find.hint: Look at the last letter: in the word “chelek” it looks like a hook reaching down: ק. And the first letter is ח, like a gate.
find.task: Find all 8 of these words. Careful: “futility,” הֶבֶל, is hiding nearby.
find.done: All eight are found! The word “portion” is hidden in the book exactly that many times.
puzzle.pieces: What comes to you more easily than to others.
What you are like: brave, calm, persistent, kind.
What you can think about for hours.
Everything you have already lived through and learned. Even the hard things.
A place where someone near you needs help.
What has been entrusted to you in particular.
puzzle.hint: Start with the corners and edges: they have a straight side. Look at the colour and the pattern on each piece.
puzzle.say: Put the picture together: drag the pieces with your finger or the mouse. Pieces that fit will lock together by themselves.
puzzle.sayA: The adult version: twenty-five pieces. Drag them with your finger or the mouse, and pieces that fit will lock together by themselves. Each part of the picture will reveal its own meaning.

puzzle.done: These are the parts that make up a person's portion. And in the centre there is a question mark: this place is waiting for your piece.

mirror.say.y: All those mirrors showed other people. But this mirror is yours. Would you like to look into it? You need a camera for that.
mirror.say.t: All the mirrors in this hall showed someone else. But this mirror is yours: it shows only you. Would you like to look? You need a camera for that.

mirror.verse.y: In the mirror you saw yourself. And your Jewish name has its own verse in Tanach: it begins with the first letter of the name and ends with the last. Shall we find it?
mirror.verse.t: In the mirror you saw yourself, not someone else. Your Jewish name also has something that is only yours: its own verse in Tanach. It begins with the first letter of the name and ends with the last. No one can say it for you. Let’s find it.

mirror.privacy.y: The camera image is not sent anywhere. A photo for the certificate is saved only if you press the button yourself, only on this device and only while the game is open. If you like, ask an adult for permission.
mirror.privacy.t: The camera image is not sent anywhere. A photo for the certificate is saved only if you press the button yourself, only on this device and only while the game is open. The camera will turn off as soon as you move on.

mirror.caption: This is you: the only one like you in the whole world.

mirror.after.y: This mirror doesn't compare you with anyone. There is nobody “better” or “worse” here. Only you, with your own piece.
mirror.after.t: Notice: this mirror doesn't compare you with anyone. There is nobody “better” or “worse” in it, only you and your piece of the great puzzle.

mirror.afterNoCam: All right. Your mirror shows your hero. It doesn't compare you with anyone: here there is only you and your piece.

species.say.y: On Sukkot we take four plants together. Tap each one and put the bundle together.
species.say.t: This is why Kohelet is read precisely on Sukkot. On this festival we bind four kinds of plants together. The Midrash sees in them four types of people. Tap each plant and put the bundle together.

species.empty: The bundle is empty so far

species.end.y: The Midrash says: let everyone be bound together. The mitzvah is fulfilled only when all four are together. If even one is missing, it won't work.
species.end.t: The Midrash says: “Let them all be bound together in one bundle, and these will atone for those.” The mitzvah is fulfilled only when all four are together. If one is missing, even the aravah without taste or fragrance, the whole bundle is invalid.

sky.title: Moshe and Yehoshua

sky.text.y: Moshe was a great teacher. His student Yehoshua led the people after him. The Talmud says: “The face of Moshe is like the sun, the face of Yehoshua is like the moon.” The sages said this with sadness: people had become weaker.
sky.text.t: Moshe was a great teacher. His student Yehoshua led the people after him. In the Talmud (Bava Batra 75a) the elders said: “The face of Moshe is like the sun, the face of Yehoshua is like the moon.” They said it with bitterness: the generation had grown weaker.

sky.q: The moon shines more weakly than the sun. Does that mean it is worse?
sky.after: Rav Ashkenazi explains: at night the sun can't be seen. And the world needs precisely the light of the moon. The moon doesn't need to become the sun. It has its own time and its own work.
hands.title: Yaakov's blessing
hands.q: Menashe, the elder, is standing under his grandfather's right hand. What will Yaakov do?
hands.after: Yaakov crossed his hands. He placed his right hand on the head of the younger one, Ephraim. Yosef objected: “Not so, my father!” But Yaakov answered: “I know, my son, I know.” And he blessed the younger one first.
circles.hint: Choose quickly, don't think too long. The first thing that comes to mind is often the most accurate.
circles.say: Four circles. Tap each one and choose up to three answers. Where the circles overlap, your portion may be hiding.

sm.default: making the world around you a little better in your own way
sm.combos: creating something new and useful for others
helping others understand what is difficult
being there when someone is having a hard time
bringing people together and seeing things through to the end
finding solutions that others don't notice
filling others with energy and team spirit
sm.gift: These are not just talents. They are gifts: the Almighty gave them to you, and each of them has its own “what for.”
sm.flow: Try to pay attention to when time flies by unnoticed. You said: “{{flow}}.” That is worth exploring.
sm.rabbi: Rabbi Shneor Ashkenazi told how he once almost stopped teaching, because only one or two hundred people watched his classes. And then he read: “Never stop doing what you are good at.” He didn't give up.
final.say: Here it is, the great puzzle. Everyone you met along the way is here. Each one in their own place. One place is missing.

final.foot: For adults: the game is based on the lesson by Rabbi Shneor Ashkenazi, “The Secret of the Book of Kohelet.” Sources: Kohelet 1:2, 1:18, 2:4–11, 3:22, 5:17–18, 9:9, 12:13; Pirkei Avot 2:16, 4:1; Bereishit 30:1, 48:14–20; Shemot 6:9; Shmuel I 15:24, 18:7–9; Esther 4:14; Vayikra Rabbah 30:12; Bava Batra 21a, 75a; Yoma 22b; Sanhedrin 90a; Rambam, Laws of the Torah Scroll 10:1. The words of the book of Kohelet belong to King Shlomo, and according to the Talmud (Bava Batra 15a) it was written down by King Chizkiyahu and his company. In the Talmud the comparison of Moshe and Yehoshua with the sun and the moon is said with bitterness; the positive reading, like the idea that Menashe “did not fight,” is Rav Ashkenazi's interpretation, and both are labelled as such in the text. Three text levels: ages 8–11, 12–15 and 16+. The child's answers are stored only in this browser.
path.reportTitle: The path through the seven worlds
path.solveText: King Shlomo tested wealth, wisdom and glory and called all of it vapour. But in his book the word חֵלֶק, “portion,” appears 8 times. The Almighty hands out the pieces: He designed the whole picture. And the last words of the book (Kohelet 12:13) say that the foundation is the same for everyone: “fear the Almighty and keep His commandments.” Happiness is not in putting together the whole puzzle. It is in finding your own piece and rejoicing in it.
path.talk: For a conversation at home or in class
path.questions: What are you so good at that time flies by unnoticed?
When were you last happy about someone else's success? What did you feel?
Who near you needs what you can do right now?
What “piece” in our family or class can only you add?
Why do you think the Almighty gave you precisely your piece?

about.title: About the app
about.made: Created as part of the project {{link}}.
about.text: “The Secret of Kohelet” is an interactive adventure for children aged 8–15 and for adults (16+). Together with the Keeper of the ancient library, the child goes through seven worlds of the book of Kohelet and searches for their chelek: the portion that the Almighty gave to them in particular. The game has three versions of the texts (ages 8–11, 12–15 and 16+), four languages, voice hints and music.
about.lesson: The game is based on the lesson by Rabbi Shneor Ashkenazi, “The Secret of the Book of Kohelet.” All rights to the lesson, its content and interpretations belong to the author. Rav Ashkenazi's interpretations are marked in the text of the game.
about.music: The Chabad niggunim “Ufaratzta,” “Tzama,” “Shamil” and “Nyet, nyet, nikavo” from the collection “Nitzotzot shel Kedusha” (“Niggunei Chabad,” volumes 5–6). All rights to the recordings belong to their rights holders. The music can be turned off in the menu.
about.code: The puzzle runs on the open-source libraries headbreaker (ISC licence) and Konva (MIT licence). The Keeper's voice was recorded in advance with Microsoft Azure AI Speech; whatever is not in the recording (for example, the hero's name) is read by the browser's voice. The verses in “Your verse in Tanach” come from the list “פסוק המתחיל ומסתיים באות” of the Torat Emet library (toratemetfreeware.com); the index of names is based on the Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (licence CC BY 4.0). “Hayom Yom” is a book of the Lubavitcher Rebbe; the text is in Hebrew. Fonts Unbounded, Onest and Frank Ruhl Libre — SIL Open Font License 1.1.
about.privacy: Your answers, name and photo are not sent anywhere: progress, answers and settings are stored only on this device, and you can erase them with “Start over”. The game uses no third-party services: all its files, fonts included, load only from this site (like any website it is hosted somewhere — on GitHub Pages, which sees the device's IP address when the page loads). The camera in the Mirror world turns on only when you press the button, the microphone is never used, and the image is not recorded. A photo for the certificate is saved only when you press the button, only on this device and only while the game is open: it is erased when you close the tab, and before that you can delete it on the certificate screen. Only the admin sign-in (uploading pictures for verses) talks to GitHub, using the admin’s own key; players never make such requests.
lesson.title: Book an online lesson
lesson.h: A lesson on “The Secret of Kohelet” with a real teacher
lesson.text: We offer an online lesson based on this game, in one or two sessions. The author of the project teaches these lessons himself: together we walk through the worlds of the Book of Kohelet, talk about the questions, and everyone looks for their own chelek.
lesson.format: One or two online sessions. One-to-one or in a group: a class, a family, a club, a community.
lesson.who: A teacher with many years of experience. Students of any age are welcome – children, teens and adults; individual and group lessons.
lesson.contact: Write to {{mail}}: tell us how many participants there will be and how old they are, and we will agree on a time.

pasuk.title: Your verse in Tanach
pasuk.lead: Every Jewish name has its own verse in Tanach: it begins with the first letter of the name and ends with the last. Write your name in Hebrew and find your verse.
pasuk.custom: There is a custom: at the end of the Amidah, before the second “Yihyu leratzon”, one says a verse that begins and ends with the letters of one’s name, or a verse with the name itself in it. It is said that this way the soul remembers its name forever.

lot.sheetEmpty: Enter your Hebrew name or your birthday, and your sheet will appear here.
lot.quest: Now you know where your lot is written. What you do with it unfolds in the seven worlds of the Book of Kohelet.
lot.src: The verse comes from the Torat Emet list, the word of the day from the Lubavitcher Rebbe’s book “Hayom Yom”. The portion of your birth is the one read on the Shabbat of your birthday or the next Shabbat after it; if that Shabbat was a festival, the portion before. Your name and date stay on this device only.
hy.yHint: Needed only for the portion of your birth. For example, 5770 is 2009/2010.
hy.placeHint: In Israel and outside Israel the weekly portions are sometimes a week apart.
sheet.parshaNote: The weekly portion of the week I was born.

Repository access: Only select repositories → TeacherRG/Koelet.

board.s: A board with seven worlds, question squares and help squares. Everyone plays together and everyone wins together.

rules.s: How to play, station tasks, six hero tokens, seven puzzle pieces and a paper die.

cards.s: 12 conversation cards. The questions depend on age.

memory.s: 16 cards: a quote in Hebrew and its translation. Find which goes with which.

piece.s: A sheet for thinking about your chelek: what I can do, what I love, whom I can help.

family.s: 12 pieces: everyone writes on their own piece what they bring to the family. On Shabbat you put it together.

shab.board.sub: A board game for the whole family. 2–6 players, a die and tokens. The rules are on the next sheet.

shab.board.legend.q: Question: take a card and answer
shab.board.legend.h: Help: move someone behind you 2 squares forward
shab.board.legend.l: Light: tell what was good this week

shab.rules.h: How to play “The Path of Kohelet”
shab.rules.need: You need: the board, the tokens and seven puzzle pieces (cut them out below), a die (an ordinary one or the paper one from this sheet) and the “Questions for the Shabbat table” cards.
shab.rules.list: Everyone puts their token on “Start”. Take turns: roll the die and move that many squares.
“?” square: take the top card and answer the question. The others may add to it. There are no right or wrong answers.
Heart square: move anyone who is behind you 2 squares forward. If nobody is behind you, move 2 squares forward yourself.
Candles square: tell what was good for you this week.
World station: everyone stops here, even if the die shows more. Do the station task from the list below. Whoever reaches the station first puts a puzzle piece on it.
The game ends when everyone has reached the finish and all seven pieces lie on the board. Everyone wins together: just like a puzzle, the picture is only complete with every piece.
shab.rules.st: Name one thing that makes you happy for longer than a day.
Say which piece you bring to our family.
Tell the person on your left what they are good at.
What would you like to learn from someone at this table?
Name your tool: what are you best at?
Tell whom you help and who helps you.
Name one small step you will take next week.
shab.rules.tokens: Tokens: cut out and fold in half along the dashed line
shab.rules.die: Die: cut out, fold along the lines and glue
shab.cards.sub: Cut out the cards before Shabbat and put them in a pile. There are no right or wrong answers here: every voice is worth hearing.

shab.cards.list.y: If you had absolutely everything in the world, what would you still be missing?
shab.cards.list.t: King Shlomo had everything, and still he said: “All is vapour.” Why does wealth alone not fill a person?
shab.cards.list.a: Kohelet calls everything “hevel”, vapour. What in your life turned out to be vapour, and what has stayed for a long time?

shab.cards.list.y: What kind of joy happens only on Shabbat?
shab.cards.list.t: How is the joy of a new thing different from the joy of helping someone?
shab.cards.list.a: Maslow put self-actualisation at the top of the pyramid. How is chelek, the portion given by the Almighty, different from “actualising yourself”?

shab.cards.list.y: Imagine a puzzle with one piece missing. What is wrong with it?
shab.cards.list.t: “It is not your duty to finish all the work, but neither are you free to withdraw from it.” Which part of the work is yours?
shab.cards.list.a: Pirkei Avot 2:16: “It is not your duty to finish the work, but neither are you free to withdraw from it.” Where do you feel this freedom and this responsibility?

shab.cards.list.y: Who at this table is a little like you? And how are you different?
shab.cards.list.t: Why did the Almighty create people so different, and not all the same?
shab.cards.list.a: What would the world lose if all people were equally gifted in the very same thing?

shab.cards.list.y: Tell the person on your right what they are good at.
shab.cards.list.t: When you compare yourself with others, do you feel better or worse? Why?
shab.cards.list.a: Social media shows the best moments of other people’s lives. How do you avoid measuring your portion with someone else’s ruler?

shab.cards.list.y: Yaakov blessed the younger brother first, and the brothers did not quarrel. How did they manage that?
shab.cards.list.t: Efraim and Menashe did not argue about who was more important. Why are children blessed with their names on Friday night?
shab.cards.list.a: Rav Ashkenazi explains: Menashe “did not fight” for first place. When is giving way a strength, and when is it a weakness?

shab.cards.list.y: Rachel envied her sister’s good deeds and began to do more good herself. Can envy be useful?
shab.cards.list.t: “The envy of scholars increases wisdom.” When does envy help you grow, and when does it get in the way?
shab.cards.list.a: Shaul wanted David to have less; Rachel wanted to have more herself. How can you tell which kind of envy is speaking in you?

shab.cards.list.y: Which tool would be yours: a hammer, a brush, a violin or a book? Why?
shab.cards.list.t: What comes easily to you, even though it is hard for others?
shab.cards.list.a: Which talent of yours did you not notice for a long time, until someone pointed it out?

shab.cards.list.y: What do you love doing so much that you forget the time?
shab.cards.list.t: What can you do, what do you love, and who needs it? Where do these three circles meet?
shab.cards.list.a: Have you ever looked for your chelek in one place and found it somewhere completely different?

shab.cards.list.y: Queen Esther was in the palace at just the right time to save her people. Remember a time when your help came at just the right moment.
shab.cards.list.t: “Who knows whether it was not for a time like this that you are here?” What might you be here for right now?
shab.cards.list.a: “And who knows whether it was not for a time like this that you attained royalty?” (Esther 4:14). What “time like this” has there been in your life?

shab.cards.list.y: “Who is rich? One who rejoices in his portion.” What are you happy about today?
shab.cards.list.t: Does rejoicing in your portion mean sitting still and doing nothing? Or the opposite?
shab.cards.list.a: “Who is rich? One who rejoices in his portion” (Pirkei Avot 4:1). How can you rejoice in what is yours and still keep growing?

shab.cards.list.y: What good deed will you do next week?
shab.cards.list.t: Which one small step this week will make your puzzle piece shine brighter?
shab.cards.list.a: If one line were written about your portion in the world, what would you like it to say?

shab.memory.sub: Cut out the 16 cards and lay them face down. Take turns turning over two at a time: a pair is a quote in Hebrew and its translation. When a pair is found, read the translation aloud.

shab.memory.pairs.tr: “Futility of futilities, all is futile.” Literally: “all is vapour.”
“It is not your duty to finish all the work.”
“Who is rich? One who rejoices in his portion.”

shab.memory.pairs.he: כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
shab.memory.pairs.tr: “All Israel have a portion in the World to Come.”
“And who knows whether it was not for a time like this…”

shab.piece.sub: Fill it in before Shabbat, and at the Shabbat table tell everyone about your piece. Chelek is the portion the Almighty gave to you in particular.
shab.piece.name: Name
shab.family.sub: Before Shabbat: everyone takes one piece, writes their name on it and draws or writes what they bring to the family. Then cut the sheet along the lines. On Shabbat put the puzzle together: the picture is only complete with every piece.
shab.family.name: Name
voice.shabbat: Here are sheets to print for Shabbat: a board game, conversation cards and the “Find the Pair” game. Choose the sheets and tap “Print”.
voice.hayom: Here you can find out what the Rebbe wrote in the book “Hayom Yom” for your birthday. Enter the regular or the Jewish date. This is optional.
voice.pasuk: Here you will find your verse in Tanach. Check how your name is written in Hebrew: the verse begins with its first letter and ends with its last.
voice.gallery: Here your verse becomes a picture. Choose a scene and a format and download it. It is free.
voice.lot: Here are your three scrolls: the verse of your name, the word for your birthday and the portion of your birth. Below you can download a sheet with all three.
voice.lotName: Write your name in Hebrew and tap “Next”. You can skip this step.
voice.lotDate: Enter your birthday and where you were born, then tap “Open the scrolls”. This is optional.
